guia.what: Switches between related views within the same context. It exposes the selected value—each tab declares its own (`data-ts-value`), and the matching panel is shown. It has variants and a vertical orientation (`orientation-vertical`).
whenUse: They’re alternate views of the same object, like details, activity, and settings.
Only one makes sense at a time, and switching is cheap.
Users don’t need to compare two views at the same time.
whenAvoid: It’s a form value, not a view → `segmented-control`.
They’re separate pages with their own URL → `nav-bar` or `sidebar`.
The content is best read in full, top to bottom → `accordion` or plain sections.
dos: Short labels that say what’s inside.
Few tabs. If they don’t fit on one line, this isn’t the right component.
donts: Don’t hide something the user always needs to see in a tab.
Don’t use them for the steps of a process. Steps have an order; tabs don’t.

teclado.action: In a horizontal tablist (`orientation-horizontal`) they switch to the next and previous tab, wrapping around. On an RTL page they swap: ← moves forward and → moves back. In the vertical tablist they do nothing.

In a vertical tablist (`orientation-vertical`, which exposes `aria-orientation="vertical"`) they switch to the next and previous tab. In the horizontal one they do nothing and the page keeps scrolling.
Leaves the tablist. The active tab is the only tab stop, and the next one is the panel (`tabindex="0"`).

nucleo: Core switches the active panel. The markup already includes `role="tab"`. Switches the active panel and keeps `aria-selected` and `tabindex` in sync. The ← and → arrow keys move between tabs (APG pattern).
